title: Low Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) and CIP — Pueblo County Department of Human Services — 320 West 10th Street - Pueblo County
summary: The Low Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) is a federally funded program designed to help qualifying low-income households cover part of their winter home heating costs from November 1st - April 30th. Once benefits are approved, LEAP can provide a financial credit directly to the heat supplier, or it can place the credit on a QUEST/EBT card to pay for a heating source such as wood, coal, propane, or for heat billed on a shared meter. May provide immediate assistance when heating source is disconnected. Also provides the Crisis Intervention Program (CIP) is designed to assist with repair of the primary heating source (i.e., furnace). Repair of furnace usually within 3 days of referral.

title: Legal Clinics - Neighborhood Call in Clinic — Pueblo County Pro Bono Project — No physical location - Pueblo County
category: Legal Aid and Civil Legal Services
summary: Neighborhood Legal Clinics provide free legal information that is informal, friendly and accessible by phone. Advanced appointments are not available. Phone number is only active on clinic dates. When you call in you will hear a message explaining the clinic. Your call will then be placed on hold for the next available lawyer. Your hold time should not be more than 10-15 minutes. If you decide not to hold you can hang up at any time. As a free community service, the clinics provide information on a wide variety of legal issues including but not limited to:  • Divorce  • Child support and custody  • Adoption  • Grandparent legal issues  • Employment  • Landlord/Tenant  • Debtor/Creditor problems  • Bankruptcy  • Consumer affairs  • Wills  • Seal criminal records and convictions  • Estate planning, and probate.

title: Care Service Program — South Central Council of Governments — 211 East Elder Street - Huerfano County
category: Medical, Dental, Vision, Hearing, and Pharmacy Services
summary: The care service program, licensed by the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, provides non-medical services in Las Animas and Huerfano Counties. It helps clients remain independent in their homes with the support of personal care providers. Services are customized to each client's needs and do not require a physician’s order or nurse supervision. Case management staff conduct an initial home assessment and collaborate with family members to create a personalized care plan. The program also offers valuable social interaction to support overall well-being and happiness. All services aim to provide peace of mind to clients and their families.

fields.eligibility: Eligibility for the Home Community-Based (Medicaid) Program is determined by the local Department of Human Services in Las Animas or Huerfano County. Once deemed eligible, individuals will be referred to the appropriate office for staffing. Eligibility for the Area Agency on Aging program requires individuals to be residents of Las Animas or Huerfano County, aged 60 and older, registered in the AAA program, and have completed an updated AAA assessment. Additional eligibility requirements may apply. Area Served: Huerfano and las animas counties
fields.access method: • Obtain a referral and authorization from the local Department of Human Services for the Home Community-Based Program (Colorado Health First/Colorado Medicaid). • Complete an in-home assessment for private pay and grant funding.
